title: Science Promising Models Wave 011 — From Broad Theory to Calculable Benchmarks
purpose: Advance the science branches with the best current combination of mathematical definition, explanatory potential and falsifiability. Wave 011 deliberately narrows broad Potatoverse theories into small benchmark models that can be solved, fitted or rejected before more complexity is added.
selection_rule: Promising means the model can explain a well-defined class of phenomena and has a credible path from equations to observables. It does not mean the model is probably true, globally novel or empirically supported already.

models.why_selected: Most direct route from recovered UPT field/Higgs language to ordinary calculable particle physics.
models.explanatory_target: A hidden scalar sector communicating with the Standard Model through the Higgs portal; provides a baseline for testing whether UPT-specific nonlocal structure adds anything.
models.next_decisive_step: Map the singlet parameter space against Higgs invisible/precision constraints and then compare the local model with one precisely defined nonlocal UPT kinetic kernel.

models.why_selected: Threshold emergence has a legitimate analogue in spontaneous scalarization, and a radion supplies a disciplined bridge from an extra scalar to compactification geometry.
models.explanatory_target: How a conventional branch can lose stability above a curvature threshold and reorganize into a new branch; under a true radion derivation, how a compactification scale could change with the branch.
models.next_decisive_step: Solve the linear zero-mode/eigenvalue onset and then require a stable nonlinear branch before attempting the 5D/radion interpretation.

models.why_selected: It maps naturally onto a genuine open empirical problem: distinguishing influence from homophily and common exposure in temporal networks.
models.explanatory_target: Why relationships form, when network exposure actually predicts later state change and when apparent contagion is only selection/common cause.
models.next_decisive_step: Pass synthetic ground-truth recovery tests before fitting any real network; then compare a joint edge/state model against homophily/common-shock baselines.

models.why_selected: The recovered equation is exact, low-dimensional and falsifiable. Its value is unusually high for testing because it fixes b rather than fitting any spiral after the fact.
models.explanatory_target: Whether a target geometry genuinely follows the project's exact quarter-turn golden self-similarity rather than merely looking spiral-like.
models.next_decisive_step: Fit one real digitized target with center uncertainty and held-out arcs against golden, free-logarithmic, Archimedean and flexible baselines.

shared_research_logic: Start with the smallest nested model.
Derive rather than name the threshold/parameter where possible.
Compare with a simpler established baseline.
Use observables that can reject the model.
Add complexity only after the simpler model is solved and its failure is understood.
Treat a successful structural analogue as support for that mathematical mechanism only, not for unrelated theological or physical claims.

models_not_prioritized_in_this_wave.reason: valuable as typed source-channel-manifestation/inverse-problem structure, but no independently motivated physical degrees of freedom currently justify turning it into a particle/field model.
storage/release mathematics is useful, but no anomalous fundamental-force observation currently motivates a new mediator/force law.
historical inputs remain unrecovered; further calculation would risk reverse-engineering a remembered output.
the historical physical pointing vector/reference frame remains unresolved, so more angular calculation would not yet answer a defined question.

relationship_to_previous_waves: Wave 009 created new deductions; Wave 010 imposed research-paper rigor and a completion matrix; Wave 011 chooses a small number of branches and turns them into nested benchmark models with explicit equations, baselines and rejection paths.
